units.name: Energy
units.summary: The forms energy takes and how it moves between them.

topics.name: Forms of Energy
topics.summary: Energy is never used up — it changes form.

lessons.title: Forms of Energy and How It Changes

objectives.text: Name the main forms of energy.
Describe an energy change in a everyday device.

keyTerms.definition: What is needed to make something happen — to move, heat or light.
Energy changing from one form to another.
Energy is never created or destroyed, only changed in form.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body: People say energy is "used up". It never is. This lesson is about what actually happens to it.

sections.heading: Forms of energy
sections.body:
Energy comes in several forms:

    LIGHT — from the sun, a lamp, a fire
    HEAT (thermal) — from a stove, the sun, your body
    SOUND — from a drum, a voice, an engine
    MOVEMENT (kinetic) — anything that is moving
    ELECTRICAL — flowing through wires
    CHEMICAL — stored in food, fuel, a battery

Stored energy is still energy. A battery sitting in a drawer doing nothing holds chemical energy the whole time.

sections.heading: Energy changes form
sections.body:
Devices do not make energy. They CHANGE it from one form to another.

    Torch:     chemical (battery) → electrical → light
    Radio:     chemical → electrical → sound
    Cooking fire: chemical (wood) → heat and light
    Your body: chemical (food) → movement and heat

Follow the arrows in the torch. The battery does not create light. It holds chemical energy, which becomes electrical energy in the wire, which becomes light in the bulb. Same energy, three forms.

sections.heading: Nothing is used up
sections.body:
When a battery "goes flat", the energy did not vanish. It left as light, a little sound, and heat — and heat spreads into the air where it is too thinly spread to be useful.

That is what "used up" really means: not destroyed, but changed into a form too spread out to use again.

This is the CONSERVATION OF ENERGY: energy is never created or destroyed, only changed in form. Add up all the energy before and after, and the totals match.
sections.example:
Where the energy goes in a torch.

Start: 100 units of chemical energy in the battery.

After running:
    about 10 units left as light
    about 90 units left as heat

Total out: 100 units. Nothing missing.

Most of it became heat, which is why a torch that has been on feels warm. The heat was not wasted in the sense of vanishing — it was wasted in the sense of not being the form you wanted.

A good device is one where most of the energy becomes the form you actually want.

sections.heading: Try it yourself
sections.body:
1. Name the energy changes when a phone is charged, then used to play music.
2. A child slides down a slide. What energy change happens, and where did the energy come from before they slid?
3. Explain why "the battery used up its energy" is not strictly correct.
4. Why does a lamp that has been on for an hour feel warm?

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body:
• Forms include light, heat, sound, movement, electrical and chemical.
• Devices change energy from one form to another; they do not create it.
• Energy is never created or destroyed — conservation of energy.
• "Used up" means changed into heat spread too thin to use.

questions.question: What energy change happens in a torch?
questions.explanation: The battery holds chemical energy, which becomes electrical energy in the wires, which becomes light at the bulb. The torch does not create light — it changes energy that was already stored from one form into another.

questions.question: A battery "goes flat". What has actually happened to its energy?
options: It changed into light, sound and heat that spread into the surroundings
questions.explanation: Energy is never destroyed — this is conservation of energy. It became light, a little sound, and heat, and the heat spread into the air where it is too thinly spread to be useful. "Used up" means changed into a form you cannot use again, not gone.
